channel.title: Nanook Blog
channel.description: The best place to stay up-to-date with the latest Nanook news and events.

item.title: Rules Need Exit Codes, and Green Is Not Useful: What Still Went Wrong
item.description: Five bypassed test hooks, eight unnoticed red CI runs, features built correctly and pointless. Why rules need exit codes, and what I would do again.

item.title: The Agent That Pleases: Absences, Lying Instruments, and Invented Evidence
item.description: Four ways an AI coding agent fails while reporting success: accommodating tests, absent features, lying instruments, invented evidence. Incidents and rules.

item.title: Working Through 1,200 Plans: A Pipeline, a Ledger, and Many Repositories
item.description: How an autonomous agent pipeline worked through 1,240 plans across 74 repositories: a crash-safe ledger, release cascades, parallel sessions in one checkout.

item.title: Tests First, Then "Implement All Plans": Designing Services an Agent Can Verify
item.description: Design a service an AI agent can verify without Kafka or Postgres, write all tests first, prove 245 are red for the same reason, then let the agent implement.

item.title: A Service in Eleven Days, with an AI Agent and Tables That Contradict
item.description: An event-driven service in eleven days with an AI agent: 806 tests, 214 generated cases, and the eight requirement defects the tables found before any code.

item.title: A Table Cannot Stay Silent: Finding Contradictions in Requirements Before Any Code Exists
item.description: Prose stays silent where the work is; a table cannot. How translating a specification into decision tables found eight defects before any code existed.

item.title: What the Next Session Knows: A Knowledge Base and a Memory of Lessons
item.description: An AI agent session starts empty. Two stores decide what the next one knows: a knowledge base and a memory of 327 lessons in about twenty failure classes.

item.title: One Root, Many Repositories: A Directory Layout and a Requirements Lifecycle for Agent Work
item.description: A directory layout for agent work, for a multi-product SaaS and for microservices, and the lifecycle a requirement passes through from analysis to done.

item.title: Fewer Skills, Shorter Rules: Setting Up a Coding Agent That Does Not Drown in Its Own Instructions
item.description: Skills, MCP servers and an instruction file for a coding agent: 14 unused skills archived, 170 lines of rules that load themselves, and what the budget taught.

item.title: The Agent Writes the Code. Everything Around It Decides Whether You Can Trust It.
item.description: Agentic software development, measured: nine months, 74 repositories, an agent writing nearly all the code. Part 1 of a series on what makes it trustworthy.

item.title: Testing E-Invoices for 40 Country/Format Combinations
item.description: Forty country/format combinations, 35,117 equivalence classes, and eight fields our API accepted but never wrote. Testing against the specification, not our own code.

item.title: One Login Form, Eight Test Cases: A Worked Example
item.description: A complete worked example: one prompt, one decision table, eight generated test cases with real data. Everything shown is output from an actual run.

item.title: How We Test a SaaS Application with Nanook
item.description: A field report from our own products: 16 hand-written spec files replaced by 117 decision tables and 1,981 data-driven cases, run by a single runner that reads the tables as data — with the numbers, the defects it surfaced, and what decision tables do not solve.

item.title: Introducing Nanook-Table
item.description: We are proud to introduce Nanook-Table. This is the first 'official' version of Nanook-Table. It has been used about one year now in a productive environment.
